sheets.title: Early medieval kings (750 – 1200)
sheets.intro: Pratiharas, Palas, Rashtrakutas, Cholas, Chalukyas, Hoysalas and the Turks.

rows.v: Beat Chakrayudha of Kannauj; beaten by Rashtrakuta Govinda III
Bhagavati devotee; Gwalior prashasti (Mihira Bhoja) tells his wins
Beat Palas; checked Arabs of Sind; lost to Rashtrakuta Krishna II
Arab trader Sulaiman: praises his cavalry and security; Gwalior prashasti
About 750 – 770; Bengal; chosen by chiefs to end anarchy (matsyanyaya)
Won Kannauj, installed Chakrayudha; beaten by Nagabhata II and Dhruva (Rashtrakuta)
Allowed Sailendra king of Java to build a monastery at Nalanda
Overthrew Chalukya Kirtivarman II, about 753; Hiranyagarbha rite
Kailasa temple at Ellora, cut from one rock
Beat Nagabhata II and Dharmapala; reached the Himalaya; took Kanchi
Jain patron; Ellora work went on
Wrote Kavirajamarga (first Kannada poetics); Ratnamalika; Jinasena (Adipurana), Mahaviracharya (Ganitasarasangraha)
Sulaiman: one of four great kings of the world
Won Takkolam 949 over Chola Rajaditya; took Kanchi and Tanjore
Beat Pallava Aparajita at Tirupurambiyam (about 897); took Tondaimandalam
Built Shiva temples along the Kaveri
Took Madurai (Madurantaka); lost to Krishna III at Takkolam 949
Uttaramerur inscriptions: village assembly elections by lot (kudavolai)
Took Kerala (Kandalur Salai), Pandya, Gangapadi, Vengi, north Sri Lanka (Anuradhapura), Maldives
Land survey; Valanadu and nadu divisions; Strong navy; gold kasu coins
Tevaram collected by Nambi Andar Nambi
Brihadisvara (Rajarajesvaram) temple, Thanjavur, 1010; Gave land to Buddhist Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam
Took all Sri Lanka; sent army to Ganga (Pala Mahipala); raided Srivijaya, 1025
Chola navy on Bay of Bengal
Titles: Gangaikonda, Kadaramkondan; temple at Gangaikondacholapuram
United Vengi and Chola; lost Sri Lanka
Took Talakad from Cholas, 1116: title Talakadugonda
Became Vaishnava under Ramanuja; Chennakeshava temple, Belur
Took coastal Andhra up to Nellore; beat Yadavas
Motupalli abhayasasanam: protection and tax relief for sea merchants; Tanks (Ramappa, Pakhal, Laknavaram) irrigation
Ramappa temple (1213) built by Recherla Rudra
Warangal besieged by Malik Kafur (1310) and Ulugh Khan (1323); captured
Nannaya began Andhra Mahabharatam (Adi, Sabha, part of Aranya)
17 raids: Nagarkot, Mathura, Kannauj, Somnath 1025; Beat Shahis (Anandapala) at Peshawar
Broke Somnath; built a mosque in Ghazni
Lost Tarain I 1191; won Tarain II 1192 over Prithviraj III; beat Jaichand at Chandawar 1194
Won Tarain I (1191); lost Tarain II (1192)

sheets.title: Delhi Sultans (1206 – 1526)
sheets.intro: Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi kings.

rows.v: Took Delhi, Meerut, Ranthambore for Ghori; Bakhtiyar Khalji took Bihar and Bengal (Nalanda burnt)
Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque; Adhai Din ka Jhonpra; began Qutb Minar
Beat Yildiz (Tarain 1215-16), Qabacha; Mongols (Chengiz) avoided; Bengal; Ranthambore
Iqta system; silver tanka and copper jital; Turkan-i-Chihalgani (the Forty)
Finished Qutb Minar; Sultan Ghari tomb
Revolts of nobles; killed near Kaithal
Beat Mongols; put down Mewati and Bengal revolts (Tughril)
Divine kingship: Sijda and Paibos, Nauroz festival
Devagiri 1296, Gujarat 1299, Ranthambore 1301, Chittor 1303, Malwa 1305; Malik Kafur: Warangal 1310, Dwarasamudra, Madurai 1311; Beat Mongols
Fixed prices; Diwan-i-Riyasat; Shahna-i-Mandi; Dagh and chehra; Land measured; kharaj 1/2 of produce; Diwan-i-Mustakhraj
Alai Darwaza; Siri fort; Hauz Khas tank
Khurasan and Qarachil plans failed; Revolts: Ma’bar, Bengal, Vijayanagara and Bahmani born 1336 – 47
Token (copper, bronze) coins; Doab tax; Diwan-i-Kohi (farm dept); Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi
Canals (Yamuna to Hissar); Diwan-i-Khairat; Diwan-i-Bandagan; jizya on Brahmins; Tanka and jital; 24 taxes abolished
Ashokan pillars brought to Delhi; Firoz Shah Kotla
Beat Hoysala Ballala III; took Madurai (Kumara Kampana)
Wrote Sobagina Sone, Mahanataka Sudhanidhi (Telugu); Srinatha at court
Raichur 1520 over Adil Shah; took Udayagiri 1514, Kondavidu 1515, Kalinga
Irrigation tanks; trade with Portuguese (Albuquerque, Goa 1510); Nayankara system

Wrote Amuktamalyada (Telugu) and Jambavati Kalyanam (Sanskrit); Ashtadiggajas: Allasani Peddana, Nandi Timmana, Dhurjati, Madayyagari Mallana, Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, Pingali Surana, Ramarajabhushanudu, Tenali Ramakrishna
Vittala and Hazara Rama temples, Hampi; Lepakshi; Gopurams at Tirupati
Built up Penugonda; Aravidu line started by his brother Tirumala
Revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq; took Goa region
Eight tarafs; mansabdari-style ranks; land measurement
Panipat I 1526 (Ibrahim Lodi; artillery, tulughma); Khanwa 1527 (Rana Sanga); Chanderi 1528; Ghaghra 1529 (Afghans)
Lost Chausa 1539 and Kannauj (Bilgram) 1540 to Sher Shah; regained Delhi 1555
Died falling from library stairs; tomb at Delhi (Haji Begum)
Rupiya (silver), dam (copper); Three crop rates; patta and qabuliyat; land measured; Sarkar-Pargana; sarais; postal horses
Rohtas fort; tomb at Sasaram; Purana Qila mosque
Panipat II 1556 (Hemu); Chittor 1568; Gujarat 1572; Haldighati 1576; Bengal; Kabul; Kashmir; Asirgarh 1601
Mansabdari: zat and sawar, 33 ranks; Zabt, Dahsala (Todar Mal); Abolished jizya 1564 and pilgrim tax; Gold mohur, silver rupiya
Navaratnas: Birbal, Todar Mal, Tansen, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Man Singh, Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana, Mulla Do Piyaza, Fakir Aziao-Din; Akbarnama, Ain-i-Akbari (Abul Fazl)
Ibadat Khana 1575; Mahzar 1579; Din-i-Ilahi 1582; Sulh-i-kul; Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid (Fatehpur Sikri); Agra fort
Mewar submitted (Amar Singh); Kangra 1620; lost Kandahar 1622; Malik Ambar resisted
Zanjir-i-Adl (chain of justice); Nur Jahan junta; Itimad-ud-Daula
Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri (autobiography); Painting: Bishandas, Mansur, Abul Hasan
Executed Guru Arjan 1606; Itimad-ud-Daula tomb (Agra); Shalimar Bagh
Took Ahmadnagar 1633; Balkh failed; lost Kandahar 1649; war of succession
Court poets and musicians; Abdul Hamid Lahori: Badshahnama
Taj Mahal (Ustad Ahmad Lahori), Red Fort, Jama Masjid Delhi, Moti Masjid, Peacock Throne
Samugarh 1658 (Dara); Purandar treaty 1665 with Shivaji; Bijapur 1686, Golconda 1687; Sambhaji executed 1689; Revolts: Jats, Satnamis, Sikhs, Rajputs
Jizya 1679; pilgrim tax; mansabdari crisis (jagir shortage)
Banned court music; Bibi ka Maqbara; Moti Masjid (Delhi Red Fort)
War with Guru Gobind Singh’s successor Banda Bahadur
Torna 1646; Afzal Khan 1659; Surat 1664; Purandar 1665; Agra escape 1666
Ashtapradhan; Chauth (1/4) and Sardeshmukhi (1/10); Land revenue by Annaji Datto’s survey; hons
Fought Mughals; captured at Sangameshwar, executed 1689
Palkhed 1728 over Nizam; Malwa and Gujarat; took Delhi outskirts 1737
Jagirs to Holkar, Scindia, Gaikwad, Bhonsle (confederacy)
Pratiharas (Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihira Bhoja) vs Palas (Dharmapala, Devapala) vs Rashtrakutas (Dhruva, Govinda III)
Pratiharas held Kannauj longest (Nagabhata II took it c. 816); all three weakened
Rajput kingdoms; door opened for the Turks
Rashtrakutas held Tondaimandalam for a time

keys.name: Mahmud of Ghazni’s raids

rows.v: Peshawar 1001 (Jayapala, Hindu Shahi), Nagarkot, Thanesar, Mathura, Kannauj 1018, Somnath 1025 (Bhima I, Solanki)
Loot temples' wealth, not to rule (only Punjab annexed)

traps: Al-Biruni came with Mahmud; Ibn Battuta came under Muhammad bin Tughlaq

rows.v: Prithviraj III Chauhan vs Muhammad Ghori

keys.name: Tarain II

rows.v: Prithviraj captured and killed; Ajmer, Delhi to Turks

traps: Chandawar 1194: Ghori beat Jaichand Gahadavala of Kannauj

rows.v: 1309 – 10, Prataparudra II (Kakatiya) – tribute; Kohinoor said to be taken
1311, Pandyas (civil war); Kafur built a mosque at Rameswaram (Ferishta)

keys.name: Panipat I

rows.v: Artillery (Ustad Ali, Mustafa), tulughma flank, araba carts

traps: Babur used artillery first in north India at Panipat I

rows.v: Guns; Babur called it jihad, took title Ghazi, gave up wine
1539, Bihar – Sher Khan beat Humayun; Sher Khan took title Sher Shah
1540 – Humayun lost again; fled to Persia (Shah Tahmasp)
Sur rule 1540 – 1555; Humayun back after Machhiwara and Sirhind (1555)
Akbar (Bairam Khan) vs Hemu (Adil Shah Sur’s general, "Vikramaditya")
Hemu hit in the eye by an arrow

keys.name: Talikota (Rakshasa-Tangadi)

rows.v: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar vs Vijayanagara (Rama Raya)
Deccan alliance; two Muslim generals of Vijayanagara deserted
Aravidu kings moved to Penugonda, Chandragiri

traps: Berar did not join the alliance

keys.name: Haldighati

rows.v: Man Singh (for Akbar) vs Maharana Pratap (Hakim Khan Sur with him)
Mughals won, but Pratap escaped (horse Chetak)
Pratap won back much of Mewar by 1597

traps: Akbar was not present at Haldighati

keys.name: Samugarh

rows.v: Aurangzeb and Murad vs Dara Shikoh
Aurangzeb took the throne; Shah Jahan jailed in Agra fort

traps: Dharmat 1658 came first (Aurangzeb beat Jaswant Singh)

rows.v: Delhi sacked; took Peacock Throne and Kohinoor
Ahmad Shah Abdali raids; Panipat III 1761
Ahmad Shah Abdali vs Marathas (Sadashivrao Bhau)
Maratha supply cut; Rohilla and Awadh with Abdali
British rise in the north; Peshwa Balaji Bajirao died soon
12 Vishnu saints; Andal only woman; Nalayira Divya Prabandham (compiled by Nathamuni)
63 Shiva saints; Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar, Manikkavachakar; Tevaram, Tiruvachakam; Karaikkal Ammaiyar woman
Sang in Tamil, not Sanskrit; rejected caste in worship

keys.name: Acharyas

rows.v: 788 – 820; Kaladi (Kerala); Advaita; 4 mathas – Sringeri, Puri, Dwarka, Joshimath
1479 – 1531; Telugu family, born Champaran; Shuddhadvaita; Pushtimarga
12th c.; minister of Bijjala (Kalachuri); Lingayat / Virashaiva; vachanas; Anubhava Mantapa

traps: Advaita = Shankara; Vishishtadvaita = Ramanuja; Dvaita = Madhva; Shuddhadvaita = Vallabha

rows.v: 14th – 15th c.; Ram bhakti; disciples of all castes – Kabir, Raidas, Sena, Dhanna, Pipa
1440 – 1518; weaver; nirguna; dohas; Bijak; Sakhis in Guru Granth
Tailor saint; verses in Guru Granth

keys.name: Sufi orders

rows.v: Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer, came c. 1192); Bakhtiyar Kaki (Delhi); Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar (Pakpattan); Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi – "saw 7 sultans"; disciple Amir Khusrau); Salim Chishti (Fatehpur Sikri). Sama (music), kept away from courts
Bahauddin Zakariya (Multan); took state posts and grants
Khwaja Baqi Billah; Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi (orthodox, opposed Akbar)
Khanqah (hospice), pir/murshid (master), murid (pupil), silsila (chain), dargah, urs

keys.name: Sultanate government

rows.v: Land revenue assignment to officers (muqti); started by Iltutmish
Wazir (finance – Diwan-i-Wizarat), Diwan-i-Arz (army, Balban), Diwan-i-Insha (letters), Diwan-i-Risalat (religion)
Market control (Shahna-i-Mandi), dagh (branding), huliya, kharaj = 1/2 produce, measured land

traps: Diwan-i-Arz = Balban; Diwan-i-Kohi = Muhammad bin Tughlaq

keys.name: Mughal government

rows.v: Akbar 1573 – 74; zat (rank) and sawar (horse); dah-bisti; Jahangir – du-aspa sih-aspa
Zabti / Dahsala (Raja Todar Mal, 1580) – average of 10 years; land classes polaj, parauti, chachar, banjar
Vakil, Wazir/Diwan (revenue), Mir Bakshi (army, mansabs), Sadr-us-Sudur (religion, grants), Mir Saman (household)
Pay by land revenue (jagirdar); khalisa = crown land

traps: Dahsala = Todar Mal under Akbar, built on Sher Shah’s system
